purpose: Research notes for opening coaching, not a source implementation or a playing-strength claim.
evidence_scope: Official Chess.com opening pages opened on the stated date. All prose below is original short paraphrase; no database percentages are adopted.

sources.title: Sicilian Defense
sources.facts: Black uses the c-pawn to contest d4. Early d4 and the c-pawn exchange distinguish the Open treatment; Nc3 can delay that commitment.
sources.caution: Do not label every Nc3 position permanently closed, or assume every Sicilian involves opposite-side castling.
sources.verification: Official opening page opened and relevant text read; no forum/blog or search snippet relied upon.

sources.title: French Defense
sources.facts: The e6 move supports a later d5 challenge. Advance structures often give White kingside space and Black queenside activity; Exchange structures differ.
sources.caution: The blocked c8 bishop is an initial tradeoff, not proof that the bishop remains inactive in the reviewed position.
sources.verification: Official opening page opened and relevant text read; no forum/blog or search snippet relied upon.

sources.title: Caro-Kann Defense
sources.facts: The c6 move supports d5 without initially obstructing the c8 bishop. Classical, Advance and Exchange lines can produce different structures.
sources.caution: The bishop's initial freedom does not prove it actually developed outside the pawn chain.
sources.verification: Official opening page opened and relevant text read; no forum/blog or search snippet relied upon.

sources.title: Italian Game
sources.facts: Bc4 develops toward f7 while helping White prepare castling. Later c3/d4 can open the center; d3 systems often maneuver first.
sources.caution: Bc4 is not automatically a present attack on f7 if the diagonal later becomes blocked.
sources.verification: Official opening page opened and relevant text read; no forum/blog or search snippet relied upon.

sources.title: Ruy Lopez Opening
sources.facts: Bb5 targets the knight on c6 and indirectly pressures e5. Black has numerous central and developmental responses.
sources.caution: Exchanging on c6 does not automatically win e5. Do not call the pressure a forced material win.
sources.verification: Official opening page opened and relevant text read; no forum/blog or search snippet relied upon.

sources.title: Scotch Game
sources.facts: An early d4 challenges Black's central pawn. After the usual exchange and knight recapture, Black can develop against e4 or the d4 knight.
sources.caution: Gambit branches do not necessarily recapture immediately; describe recapture conditionally.
sources.verification: Official opening page opened and relevant text read; no forum/blog or search snippet relied upon.

sources.title: Petrov's Defense
sources.facts: Black's second knight move attacks e4 in reply to pressure on e5. Central exchanges and efficient development are recurring ideas.
sources.caution: Petrov, Petroff and Russian Game are aliases. Its solid reputation does not predict a draw.
sources.verification: Official opening page opened and relevant text read; no forum/blog or search snippet relied upon.

sources.title: Queen's Gambit
sources.facts: White's c-pawn challenges Black's d5 pawn. Accepted and declined responses differ in how Black maintains or releases the central tension.
sources.caution: The QGA paragraph contains a cxd4 typo; the dedicated Accepted page correctly gives dxc4. No numerical win rates from this article are used.
sources.verification: Official opening page opened and relevant text read; no forum/blog or search snippet relied upon.

sources.title: Queen's Gambit Declined
sources.facts: The dedicated page confirms d4 d5 c4 e6. The parent Queen's Gambit page explains the e6 support and a typical later c5 counterstrike.
sources.caution: This short dedicated page does not independently document all middlegame plans; plan attribution also includes the parent page.
sources.verification: Official opening page opened and relevant text read; no forum/blog or search snippet relied upon.

sources.title: Queen's Gambit Accepted
sources.facts: Black exchanges the central d-pawn for c4, freeing piece development. White can recover the pawn while making use of the center.
sources.caution: Black usually values activity over retaining the extra pawn; this is not a claim that every attempt to retain it loses.
sources.verification: Official opening page opened and relevant text read; no forum/blog or search snippet relied upon.

sources.title: Slav Defense
sources.facts: The c6 pawn supports d5 while initially keeping the c8 bishop's diagonal available. Adding e6 can enter a Semi-Slav structure.
sources.caution: An initial free bishop is not the same as a bishop already outside the pawn chain. Exchange and Semi-Slav branches need different wording.
sources.verification: Official opening page opened and relevant text read; no forum/blog or search snippet relied upon.

sources.title: London System
sources.facts: White commonly develops Bf4 before e3, then supports d4 with a compact structure. Black can challenge the center or use a kingside fianchetto.
sources.caution: The Jobava branch develops Nc3, so a universal c3-pawn prescription is wrong. The setup still depends on Black's responses.
sources.verification: Official opening page opened and relevant text read; no forum/blog or search snippet relied upon.

sources.title: King's Indian Defense
sources.facts: Black lets White occupy more central space and plans a later challenge. Closed main lines can feature attacks on different wings.
sources.caution: The page's early g6 starting position is shared with other Indian defenses. Do not infer a closed center or forced kingside attack before the actual pawn choices.
sources.verification: Official opening page opened and relevant text read; no forum/blog or search snippet relied upon.

sources.title: Nimzo-Indian Defense
sources.facts: Bb4 pins Nc3 in the characteristic starting position, reducing support for e4. Trading on c3 can exchange bishop-pair potential for structural targets.
sources.caution: Neither doubled c-pawns nor White's bishop pair exists merely because the opening is named Nimzo-Indian; verify the exchange and recapture.
sources.verification: Official opening page opened and relevant text read; no forum/blog or search snippet relied upon.

sources.title: Gruenfeld Defense
sources.facts: Black's d5 strike distinguishes this family from the related kingside fianchetto setups. In Exchange lines, Black pressures White's broad center, especially d4.
sources.caution: Accept Grunfeld, Gruenfeld and Grünfeld spellings. The Exchange pawn center is not present in every branch.
sources.verification: Official opening page opened and relevant text read; no forum/blog or search snippet relied upon.

sources.title: Reti Opening
sources.facts: Chess.com calls 1.Nf3 the Reti Opening, while acknowledging Zukertort as another name. Later pawn moves can reach English, queen-pawn or Sicilian positions.
sources.caution: A game that starts with Nf3 need not retain a Reti plan. 1.Nf3 d5 2.c4 is specifically the Reti Gambit.
sources.verification: Official opening page opened and relevant text read; no forum/blog or search snippet relied upon.

sources.title: English Opening
sources.facts: White begins with c4 and controls the center from the flank. Black's e5 or c5 responses lead to distinct families; d4 can transpose elsewhere.
sources.caution: Reversed Sicilian is an analogy with an extra White tempo, not the identical position with the same side to move.
sources.verification: Official opening page opened and relevant text read; no forum/blog or search snippet relied upon.

sources.title: King's Pawn Opening
sources.facts: The e4 move contests central squares and clears development routes. Later choices by both players determine the named defense or open-game branch.
sources.caution: A broad first-move label does not establish the later central structure.
sources.verification: Official opening page opened and relevant text read.

sources.title: King's Pawn Opening
sources.facts: The page confirms the exact initial sequence e4 e5 under this display name.
sources.caution: The page has no strategic prose. Open Game is a broad descriptive family label rather than this page's exact title.
sources.verification: Official opening page opened; title and move sequence read.

families.white: Use your central space to develop quickly. Decide whether to open the center with d4 or keep it flexible.
families.black: Your c-pawn contests d4. Develop toward the center and look for counterplay before White's attack gathers speed.
families.requires: Actual c5 response or an equivalent verified position; a Reti Sicilian Invitation alone is insufficient.

families.canonical_san: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4
families.white: The open center rewards fast development. Put your pieces to work before launching a pawn attack.
families.black: The c-file offers a route for your rooks. Challenge White's center while developing active pieces.
families.requires: Verify the d-pawn/c-pawn exchange and current structure; do not infer from Nf3 alone.

families.canonical_san: e4 c5 Nc3 Nc6 g3 g6 Bg2 Bg7
families.white: A common plan is a kingside buildup while keeping the center intact. Watch for Black's counterplay before advancing.
families.black: White has delayed d4. Develop flexibly and look for a central break or queenside counterplay.
families.requires: Nc3 may identify the catalog branch, but the closed-structure plan is conditional on the later center.

families.white: Decide how to handle the central tension. If you advance e5, use the extra space without neglecting your pawn chain.
families.black: Challenge White's center and find a useful route for the light-squared bishop. A closed center calls for well-timed pawn breaks.
families.requires: Distinguish Advance/Exchange structures; no blanket closed-center claim.

families.white: Use your room in the center to develop smoothly. Choose between maintaining, advancing or exchanging the e-pawn.
families.black: Support d5 and develop without letting the solid structure become passive. When possible, free the light-squared bishop before closing its diagonal.
families.requires: d5 may be planned after c6 rather than already played; use actual evidence tense.

families.white: Develop toward the center and get your king safe. Pick a central plan before spending moves on a flank attack.
families.black: Match White's development and keep an eye on the central pawns. The next piece moves will determine the opening's character.
families.requires: Fallback only when no more specific supported family applies.

families.white: Develop quickly and castle. You can build toward d4, or use d3 to prepare that central break more slowly.
families.black: Finish development and contest the center. Keep f7 secure and be ready when White challenges with d4.
families.requires: Identify actual Bc4 development; do not claim a current unobstructed f7 attack without checking the board.

families.white: Pressure the center through the c6 knight while developing and castling. Treat e5 as a target to build toward, not a free pawn.
families.black: Develop and keep the center coordinated. Choose how to meet the bishop's pressure before committing the pawn structure.
families.requires: Actual characteristic position or supported transposition; names like Berlin are subclasses, not a separate White opening.

families.white: You challenge the center early. Use the resulting open lines for development, and make sure e4 stays adequately protected.
families.black: Develop with pressure against White's center. After Nxd4, consider how your pieces can target e4 or the central knight.
families.requires: Recapture-dependent wording must remain conditional for gambit branches.

families.white: Develop actively after the central exchanges. Look for useful piece activity rather than assuming the symmetrical start must stay equal.
families.black: Counterattack e4 while developing. Calculate the pawn exchanges carefully instead of copying White's moves automatically.
families.requires: Petrov/Petroff/Russian Game aliases; do not misclassify as Italian due to a later Bc4.

families.white: Use c4 to challenge Black's central foothold. Develop while deciding whether exchanging or keeping the tension helps your center.
families.black: Choose how to meet the pressure on d5. Supporting the pawn and exchanging it lead to different middlegame plans.
families.requires: Prefer Accepted/Declined/Slav subclass when enough actual moves support it.

families.white: Keep pressure on the center as you develop. Watch how Black frees the light-squared bishop and prepares a pawn break.
families.black: Your e-pawn supports d5. Develop the pieces and look for a well-prepared c5 break against White's center.
families.requires: Do not prescribe a minority attack unless the actual Exchange structure supports it.

families.white: Develop around your central pawns and recover c4 when it fits. Avoid wasting time chasing the pawn with your queen.
families.black: Use the cleared center to develop actively. Be willing to return the pawn rather than tie your pieces down defending it.
families.requires: Actual dxc4 from the characteristic QG position; generic pawn capture on c4 is insufficient.

families.white: Develop behind your central pawns and prepare a useful central break. The timing depends on how Black places the light-squared bishop.
families.black: Keep d5 supported while getting your pieces out. Decide when the light-squared bishop should develop before committing to e6.
families.requires: If e6 has already blocked the bishop, describe that actual restriction or use Semi-Slav wording.

families.white: Develop the dark-squared bishop before closing its diagonal. Build a supported center, then choose an active plan against Black's setup.
families.black: Challenge d4 instead of letting White build freely. Central pressure can matter more than copying the same setup every game.
families.requires: Jobava/Nc3 branch must not be presented as a c3-pawn system.

families.canonical_san: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6
families.white: Support your broad center and develop behind it. If the center closes, choose your wing play with Black's counterattack in mind.
families.black: Develop behind the fianchettoed bishop, then challenge the center. A kingside attack is one plan when the pawn structure supports it.
families.requires: g6 alone is shared; inspect d6/d5 and whether e5/d5 actually close the center.

families.canonical_san: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4
families.white: Decide how to meet the pressure on c3. If you gain the bishop pair, look for a chance to open useful lines.
families.black: Use the pressure on c3 to restrain e4. If you exchange the bishop, make sure the resulting structure gives you worthwhile targets.
families.requires: Verify whether the pin still exists, and whether Bxc3 and a pawn recapture actually occurred.

families.canonical_san: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5
families.white: A large center is useful only if you can support it. Develop quickly so Black's pressure does not leave your pawns overextended.
families.black: Keep challenging White's central pawns. In Exchange structures, c5 and the g7 bishop often work together against d4.
families.requires: Do not substitute the closed King's Indian kingside race for this central confrontation.

families.white: Develop the knight and keep your central pawn choices open. Let Black's setup help you decide between c4, d4 and other plans.
families.black: Choose a clear central setup and develop. White's next pawn moves will tell you which structure you need to challenge.
families.requires: Latest supported transposition supersedes the initial Nf3 label; invitation names do not prove the invited defense was reached.

families.white: Control d5 from the flank and develop toward the center. Keep the d-pawn flexible until the central structure becomes clearer.
families.black: Build central control and develop naturally. Your e5, c5 or d5 setup leads to different plans, so watch White's next pawn move.
families.requires: Prefer a verified later QG/Indian family after transposition; reversed does not mean board-identical.

mapping_policy: Use the latest supported named position from actual legal standard-start history, not merely the first move or a substring in a variation name.
Opening names describe a shared position or branch reached by both players. White's choice and Black's response are explanatory roles, not independent teams in a fixed matchup table.
A catalog match can identify a historical opening even after the position departs from theory; separate that historical fact from claims about the current board.
When several catalog names share a position, preserve a stable display label and prefer evidence-backed broad plans over a guessed precise variation.
Every plan is a typical possibility, not proof that a future move is legal, good, forced or played.
Position equivalence includes piece placement, side to move, castling rights and legally available en-passant; clocks may differ. An identical diagram alone is insufficient.
Do not infer a live structural fact solely from family names: inspect pawn positions, captures, bishop development, king safety and available central breaks.
No winner is assigned from names or webpage aggregate results. Any opening-phase advantage must come from the actual reached position and explicitly bounded own-engine analysis.

targeted_regression_plan: 1.Nf3 uses the verified Reti display; Nf3 c5 alone remains an invitation, while later e4 reaches Sicilian.
Nf3 or c4 transpositions produce the same family and color plans as canonical paths at an equivalent position.
Sicilian French Variation remains Sicilian despite the word French; English Anglo-Indian remains English unless a later actual position supports the Indian family.
KID shared g6 prefix stays generic; actual d5 receives Grunfeld treatment; London versus a kingside fianchetto does not claim White has c4/e4.
Open Sicilian does not receive a closed-center plan merely because Nc3 came first.
French Exchange does not describe an e5 wedge. QGA says dxc4 rather than cxd4.
Nimzo Qxc3 does not claim doubled pawns; Nimzo before Bxc3 does not claim a bishop pair.
Slav/Semi-Slav does not assert the light-squared bishop is already free or outside the chain without actual board evidence.
London Jobava does not prescribe a pawn on c3 when its knight occupies c3.

Balance uses actual played-position evaluation at one explicit ply, white-oriented sign, sufficient exact depth; null/bounds/shallow/mismatched FEN/terminal/short-game cases do not fabricate a winner.
Opening-phase advantage and final game winner can disagree; preserve that distinction.
Both perspective views keep objective White/Black identities and only change user-relative pronouns.
Custom FEN, incomplete or malformed history, unavailable catalog and insufficient evidence degrade gracefully without invented setup claims.

implementation_audit_initial.scope: Synthetic scores test orientation and failure guards, not engine accuracy; no engine or UI.

findings.detail: Rapport-Jobava System falls back despite verified London/Jobava coverage.
Attach parent Queens-Gambit prose source for the c5 plan, since the dedicated QGD page only has the move sequence.
Present-tense summary can mention a vanished c3 knight after Nimzo Bxc3 Qxc3; use historical or actual-board wording.
Unknown-family white.name can display Black's defense name; preserve common title and use neutral per-side fallback labels.

reproduction_python:
import json,sys,copy,chess,hashlib
from pathlib import Path
src=Path('scripts/coach_openings.py')
start_bytes=src.read_bytes()
source_sha=hashlib.sha256(start_bytes).hexdigest()
sys.path.insert(0,'scripts')
from coach_openings import describe_opening
samples=json.loads(Path('docs/checks/2026-11-02-opening-coach/source-verification.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))['prepared_audit_cases']
def packet(line):
    b=chess.Board()
    for san in line.split(): b.push_san(san)
    after=b.copy(stack=True); move=b.pop()
    return b, {'ply':len(b.move_stack)+1,'uci':move.uci(),'fen_before':b.fen(en_passant='fen'),'fen_after':after.fen(en_passant='fen'),'classification':'good','played':{'uci':move.uci(),'pv_uci':[move.uci()],'bound':'exact','depth':4,'score_cp_white':75,'mate_white':None}}
def describe(line):
    b,r=packet(line)
    return describe_opening(b,r)
checks=0
for case in samples:
    b,row=packet(case['san']); old=(b.fen(),tuple(b.move_stack),copy.deepcopy(row))
    for cp in [-250,-100,-99,-50,-49,0,49,50,99,100,250]:
        row['played']['score_cp_white']=cp
        out=describe_opening(b,row)
        if len(b.move_stack)+1<12:
            assert out['assessment']['status']=='too_early' and out['assessment']['side'] is None
        else:
            assert out['assessment']['side']==('white' if cp>=50 else 'black' if cp<=-50 else None),(case['id'],cp,out['assessment'])
            expected='balanced' if abs(cp)<50 else 'slight_edge' if abs(cp)<100 else 'better_start'
            assert out['assessment']['status']==expected,(case['id'],cp,out['assessment'])
            assert out['assessment']['provisional'] is True,(case['id'],out['assessment'])
        assert out['fen']==row['fen_after'] and out['ply_index']==row['ply']
        if not case['san'].startswith('Nf3'):
            assert not out['summary'].startswith('The game began with Nf3'),case['id']
        checks+=1
    row['played']['score_cp_white']=75
    assert (b.fen(),tuple(b.move_stack),row)==old,case['id']
    checks+=1
b,base=packet('e4 e6 d4 d5 exd5 exd5 Nf3 Nf6 Bd3 Bd6 O-O O-O')
mutations={
 'missing_played':lambda x:x.pop('played'),
 'lower_bound':lambda x:x['played'].update(bound='lowerbound'),
 'upper_bound':lambda x:x['played'].update(bound='upperbound'),
 'shallow_depth':lambda x:x['played'].update(depth=3),
 'depth_boolean':lambda x:x['played'].update(depth=True),
 'score_boolean':lambda x:x['played'].update(score_cp_white=True),
 'mate_score':lambda x:x['played'].update(mate_white=3),
 'illegal_pv':lambda x:x['played'].update(pv_uci=[x['uci'],'a1a8']),
 'mismatched_root':lambda x:x['played'].update(uci='a7a6'),
 'wrong_frame':lambda x:x['played'].update(pv_frames=[{'fen':chess.STARTING_FEN},{'fen':x['fen_after']}]),
 'uncertain':lambda x:x.update(classification='uncertain'),
 'pending':lambda x:x.update(classification='pending'),
 'classification_missing':lambda x:x.pop('classification')}
for name,mutation in mutations.items():
    row=copy.deepcopy(base);mutation(row)
    out=describe_opening(b,row)
    assert out['assessment']['status']=='unavailable' and out['assessment']['side'] is None,(name,out['assessment'])
    checks+=1
for key,value in [('fen_before',chess.STARTING_FEN),('fen_after',chess.STARTING_FEN),('ply',999)]:
    row=copy.deepcopy(base);row[key]=value
    assert describe_opening(b,row) is None,key
    checks+=1
assert describe_opening(chess.Board(b.fen()),base) is None
checks+=1
bm,mr=packet('e4 e5 Bc4 Nc6 Qh5 Nf6 Qxf7#')
mate=describe_opening(bm,mr)
assert mate['assessment']['status']=='checkmate' and mate['assessment']['side']=='white'
assert mate['assessment']['provisional'] is False
checks+=1
by_id={item['id']:item for item in samples}
targeted=[]
out=describe(by_id['jobava']['san'])
assert out['white']['name']=='Rapport-Jobava System' and 'https://www.chess.com/openings/London-System' in out['sources']
targeted.append({'id':'jobava_alias','passed':True,'white_name':out['white']['name']})
out=describe(by_id['english_to_qgd']['san'])
assert {'https://www.chess.com/openings/Queens-Gambit-Declined','https://www.chess.com/openings/Queens-Gambit'}<=set(out['sources'])
targeted.append({'id':'qgd_citation','passed':True,'sources':out['sources']})
out=describe(by_id['nimzo_queen_recapture']['san'])
assert 'put pressure' in out['summary'] and 'pressures the c3-knight' not in out['summary']
targeted.append({'id':'historical_summary','passed':True,'summary':out['summary']})
out=describe(by_id['kid_shared']['san'])
assert out['white']['name']=='White setup' and out['black']['name']=='Black response'
targeted.append({'id':'fallback_side_labels','passed':True,'white':out['white'],'black':out['black']})
line='e4 c5 c3 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 cxd4 cxd4 d6 Nf3 Nc6'
out=describe(line)
assert 'Alapin' in out['recognition']['name'] and out['white']['name']!='Open Sicilian'
targeted.append({'id':'alapin_pawn_recapture','passed':True,'san':line,'white_name':out['white']['name'],'recognized_name':out['recognition']['name']})

import sys,chess,json,hashlib
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0,'scripts')
from coach_openings import describe_opening
src=Path('scripts/coach_openings.py')
source_hash=hashlib.sha256(src.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
cases=[
('closed_d2','e4 c5 Nc3 Nc6 g3 g6 Bg2 Bg7 Nge2 d6 O-O e5',chess.D2),
('closed_d3','e4 c5 Nc3 Nc6 g3 g6 Bg2 Bg7 d3 d6 Be3 e5',chess.D3),
('french_advance','e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Qb6 Bd3 Bd7',None)]
results=[]
for key,line,square in cases:
    b=chess.Board()
    for san in line.split(): b.push_san(san)
    a=b.copy(stack=True);m=b.pop()
    row={'ply':len(a.move_stack),'uci':m.uci(),'fen_before':b.fen(en_passant='fen'),'fen_after':a.fen(en_passant='fen'),'classification':'good','played':{'uci':m.uci(),'pv_uci':[m.uci()],'bound':'exact','depth':4,'score_cp_white':75,'mate_white':None}}
    out=describe_opening(b,row)
    if square is not None:
        assert a.piece_at(square)==chess.Piece(chess.PAWN,chess.WHITE)
        assert out['white']['name']=='Closed Sicilian setup'
        assert 'behind d4' in out['sections'][0]['text']
        if square==chess.D3: assert 'on d2' not in out['sections'][0]['text']
    else:
        assert out['white']['name']=='French Advance center'
        assert a.piece_at(chess.D4)==a.piece_at(chess.E5)==chess.Piece(chess.PAWN,chess.WHITE)
        assert "Black's pawn on c5 already attacks the base on d4." in out['sections'][1]['text']
    results.append({'id':key,'passed':True,'san':line,'white_name':out['white']['name'],'white_text':out['sections'][0]['text']})
assert hashlib.sha256(src.read_bytes()).hexdigest()==source_hash
print(json.dumps({'source_sha256':source_hash,'checks':results},ensure_ascii=True,indent=2))
